KAIST v0.9 demonstrates 35 kg pushing and 20 kg lifting

DRCD Lab and RAILAB combine object handling, balance and onboard visual feedback in a new research demonstration.

Humanoids Daily ↗19 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryVideos 1

From walking to handling objects

An October 19 video shows KAIST Humanoid v0.9 pushing objects weighing up to 35 kg and lifting up to 20 kg while arranging objects into the letters KAIST. DRCD Lab developed the platform with RAILAB, which developed its arms.

Coordinating contact and balance

Physical handling requires coordinated locomotion and contact: force applied through the arms changes the demands on the legs and torso. The team reports onboard visual feedback and interaction skills learned through deep reinforcement learning and human demonstrations. The video description does not fully explain how those components are combined.

Pushing and lifting are different measures

Pushing a 35 kg object does not require supporting its full weight, and resistance depends on surface conditions. That result must be separated from the 20 kg lift. The demonstration is neither a commercial payload rating nor evidence of unrestricted autonomy, and it does not establish durability under repeated production work.
